The missiles were launched after midnight, under weather conditions that helped keep the toxic gases close to the ground, leading to a large number of casualties while people were sleeping.
The attack came at a time when Ghouta was suffering from a siege imposed by the regime since the end of 2012, which restricted the entry of fuel, medicines, and medical supplies, causing medical centers and staff to face large numbers of victims with limited resources.
The network documented the suffocation deaths of 1,144 people as a result of the attack, including 1,119 civilians, among whom were 99 children and 194 women. 
The Ghouta attacks accounted for approximately 76 percent of the total victims of the chemical attacks carried out by the regime from December 2012 to May 2019.
Those who survived the attack lived to face severe respiratory and cardiovascular diseases.
Syrians mourn their dead on this day and swear to keep the memories of their fallen brothers so that no one feels remorse for the fallen regime or accuses the revolution of being unjust.

events.text:
🇷🇺🚀 Russia's fuel strikes erode Ukrainian Army's logistical flexibility and fighting capability
The Russian Army is steadily choking off Ukraine’s fuel supplies, and the recent strike on the KLO fuel depot in Brovary is yet another nail in the coffin of Ukraine’s military mobility.
On the night of August 20, Russian forces struck the KLO fuel and lubricants depot in Brovary, a city just northeast of Kiev, that was storing up to 8,000 cubic meters of fuel intended for Ukrainian forces. Footage filmed by an eyewitness at the industrial site quickly spread across social media. The depot has ceased operations, according to Ukrainian media reports, and the company said that no site employees were injured.
Building a new gas station costs around $1.2 million, while protecting it against drone attacks costs about $44,800. Ukrainian fuel station network WOG claims that fully restoring a single station can cost up to $1.6 million. Depending on the extent of the damage, repairs can take up to ten weeks.
Since April 2026, Russia has been intensively[ targeting Ukrainian gas stations](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73491), according to Ukrainian media. The extent of the damage is being downplayed by the Ukrainian side. As early as July 6, Ekonomichna Pravda reported that 200 gas stations had been hit. Despite Russia’s military campaign, Ukrainian newspapers have stubbornly continued to cite that figure through the end of August.
📌 Geography of the strikes
The strikes on fuel stations have largely followed the locations of the Ukrainian military’s main fuel hubs and key axes of the Russian advance.
Russian forces regularly [strike port infrastructure](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72561) in Ukraine’s Odessa region and the Danube area. Izmail and Reni trade ports, which became alternative routes for fuel and weapons supplies via Romania’s port of Constanta following Russian attacks in the Black Sea, have also come [under fire.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73359)
Kiev, Dnepropetrovsk, Kharkov, Sumy, and the Ukrainian-occupied parts of Donetsk, Kherson and Zaporozhye regions have also come under attack, reports say.
🛢 Fuel strikes cripple Ukrainian Army mobility
Russian military analysts stress the strategic importance of knocking out all the gas stations along the Kharkov-Dnepropetrovsk highway, a key route used by Ukrainian forces to move troops from southern Donbass to the north. Ukrainian forces are particularly active along this route during major Russian offensives, such as those in the Kharkov and Sumy regions.
The lack of fuel stations along this stretch severely complicates the Ukrainian military’s ability to redeploy units. Ukrainian forces are forced to carry their own fuel tankers, which are vulnerable to Russian airstrikes.
Strikes on fuel stations are currently the most logical way to disrupt the enemy’s fuel supply, Russian military experts argue. With virtually no major oil refineries left operating in Ukraine, aside from a few makeshift facilities, this strategy could produce results relatively quickly. Even with Western backing, Ukraine cannot make up for the fuel infrastructure knocked out of service.

🇺🇸👁 SignalGate, psalms, and paranoia: How Jennifer Hegseth became Pete’s Pentagon gatekeeper
Jennifer Hegseth may not have a Pentagon title, a military rank or even a publicly confirmed security clearance, but she has something arguably more useful in Washington: access, reports The New York Times.
Once the executive producer who helped turn her husband into a Fox News fixture, she has seamlessly evolved into something closer to her husband’s unofficial chief of staff.
According to the report she:
♦️ serves as his most influential adviser
♦️ preps him for appearances
♦️ interviews potential staff
♦️ brainstorms Defense Department videos
♦️ sits in on high-level meetings
At one meeting with British defense officials her presence reportedly made the visitors uncomfortable enough that they later held a second session without her to discuss sensitive details. 
The Pentagon insists she was there only for introductions. 
Now, she also chairs a presidential commission on military spouses. 
Jennifer has encouraged her husband’s increasingly adversarial relationship with the media, and allegedly pushed to remove Pentagon reporters who published stories unfavorable to the Secretary of War.
👉 She also maintains direct contact with members of his inner circle, while close former Fox colleague Tami Radabaugh is now Pete’s communications adviser, and, reportedly, Jennifer Hegseth’s “eyes and ears” inside the Pentagon.
Last year Jennifer was on the notorious Signal chat in which Hegseth, using a personal device and a non-secure [messaging app, shared precise strike details](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/60660) - number of aircraft, timing - hours before the short-lived campaign against the Houthis in Yemen. An uncensored journalist was on the same thread. 
The episode, quickly dubbed SignalGate, apparently left Hegseth so paranoid that[ it triggered a Pentagon housecleaning. ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/67766)
Then there’s the religious zealotry. 
Hegseth has been dialing up [the Christian rhetoric in the Iran war](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/67283), turning the Pentagon into a pulpit. Yet, for all his divine posturing, he seems utterly dependent on his wife. 
One insider claims the War Secretary likes his wife to travel with him to keep him out of trouble. Given his alleged history of heavy drinking, that might be wise.
Her outsized role has raised fresh questions about Hegseth’s leadership - already under fire over issues like the cost of the Iran war, [shrinking munitions stocks](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72941), and[ the reported mutiny aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73465).
Meanwhile, Jennifer still has quiet access to her husband’s inner sanctum, using a garage elevator that opens directly into his office suite.

events.title: Telegram
events.text:
🤥💵 Trump’s Pentagon growing more wasteful and opaque – now it wants to gut oversight
The Pentagon and the US military-industrial complex are moving to dismantle an independent testing body – potentially to the military’s own detriment.
The Office of the Director, Operational Test and Evaluation (DOT&E), created by the US Congress in 1983 as an independent adviser on operational and live-fire testing of major weapon systems to the Secretary of Defense, has seen its staff and programs trimmed under Trump.
👉 Secretary of War Pete Hegseth, who vowed to run “the most transparent Department of Defense in history", slashed the body's staff to 30 from 126, and had 90 programs removed from its oversight, according to Bloomberg.
In late July, the Pentagon also removed 25 years of weapon-testing reports from its public website, citing concerns that adversaries could use AI to identify vulnerabilities in US weapons systems.
Earlier this year, US defense officials blocked the public release of a Government Accountability Office (GAO) report on the controversial $1.6 trillion F-35 program, designating it “Controlled Unclassified Information” (CUI) and restricting public access.
The developments have coincided with Pentagon setbacks in Iran and a growing scandal over depleted US missile stocks, which reportedly sparked Trump’s ire at Hegseth.
US weapons are 'garbage'
However, the department's attempts to scale down transparency and sweep existing problems under the rug is only making things worse, analysts told Responsible Statecraft.
💬 “Pentagon careerists and corporate go-fers have been attempting to either get rid of or defang DOT&E since its inception," former GAO employee Winslow Wheeler told RS. When the body revealed weapon flaws to the public, their money flows were interrupted.
Previously, Congress and the public could see which US weapons were performing well and which were falling short, Wheeler noted. “That ability has now been mostly eliminated.” This is particularly concerning as the Trump administration pursues a growing number of costly weapons programs, including Golden Dome and others.
➡️ The fact that Trump's Pentagon decided "to hide this information is proof positive that the weapons that we're producing are garbage,” Dan Grazier, the director of the Stimson Center’s National Security Reform program, said, as qouted by RS.
Under these circumstances, it is hardly surprising that Patriot air defense systems are struggling to protect US allies in Israel, the Gulf and Ukraine – let alone the Pentagon’s chronically delayed and vastly expensive weapons programs.

🚨🇮🇷What could Iran gain from the emerging 'Sunni NATO'?
The Saudi-Pakistan-Turkey pact could potentially benefit Iran, despite being led by traditional US allies, argue experts.
What do they mean?
The defense pact is not aimed at Iran, highlights Responsible Statecraft. Iran appears to know this: Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said on August 10 that the Islamic Republic has no concerns about the[ emergence of the Mecca alliance.](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73198)
💬 "Any plan that is based on ‌the ⁠geopolitical and historical realities of the region, is comprehensive and inclusive, and correctly ​identifies the ​enemy ⁠and the threat, has a chance of ​helping to strengthen ​security ⁠and prevent instability and abuses by the Zionist enemy ⁠and ​its allies," Baghaei stressed.
The idea of establishing a Muslim defense alliance was floated by Arab countries and Turkey before the recent conflict involving Iran. Some Turkish officials even linked the idea to Israel’s growing assertiveness toward Palestine, while Saudi Arabia and Pakistan concluded a bilateral defense pact following Israel’s attack on Doha, Qatar. Some experts have drawn attention to the fact that the trilateral Mecca agreement caught Israeli intelligence agencies, as well as their Emirati counterparts, by surprise.
➡️ For Israel, this development is unsettling. For decades, Tel Aviv has sought to weaken its regional rivals and adversaries, including Iraq, Syria and Iran, while drawing Gulf monarchies into a US-backed network of security and economic ties. The apparent strategy was to prevent the emergence of a unified regional Arab front while steadily bringing Israel’s neighbors into its orbit through the Abraham Accords.
Now Israel sees Turkey, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and potentially Egypt, Qatar and Kuwait shaping a “Sunni NATO,” which some experts view as a counterweight to the [Israeli-UAE Hexagon Alliance](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/71096), or “Abraham Accords Axis.”
Iran's opportunity?
Commenting on the Saudi-Pakistani pact, Major General Yahya Rahim Safavi, then an adviser to Iran’s supreme leader, suggested in September 2025 that Iran could eventually join the agreement. “Iran, Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Iraq could move toward a collective defense pact,” he said in a televised interview.
👉 Iran may still consider joining the pact – and perhaps even more so after Turkey joined the alliance, RS argues. Why? Because Ankara proved useful in thwarting an Israel-backed incursion into Iran from Iraqi Kurdistan.
Meanwhile, the Financial Times previously reported that Saudi Arabia had been discussing a [possible peace pact between Middle Eastern players and Iran ](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/70189)at the heights of the Iran war, launched by Israel and the US.
Iran's geopolitical chess
While Iran’s formal accession to the Mecca alliance remains speculative, cooperation with its members cannot be ruled out. Both the emerging “Sunni NATO” and the Axis of Resistance view Israeli-UAE actions in the region with growing suspicion. While the Mecca pact presents itself as a more self-reliant regional security bloc, Israel and the UAE continue to favor a strong US role in regional affairs.
Moreover, Israel’s [confrontation with Turkey in Syria](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73545) and growing Saudi-UAE tensions could give Iran greater room to maneuver and exploit regional divisions.

💰📉Why ex-Soros employee’s bid to fix US economy and contain fallout from Trump’s Iran war & AI boom is doomed
The US Treasury’s push to increase buybacks of its long-term bonds to at least $4 billion is no routine move, signaling a looming US crisis and exposing divisions between two Trump proteges: ex-Soros employee and [US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/65029) and [Bilderberg darling and Fed chief Kevin Warsh](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/63714.).
What is Bessent doing?
Critics say he is manipulating the bond market to push borrowing costs back down, calling the maneuver “quantitative easing-lite". What do they mean? When the Federal Reserve creates money to buy bonds and drive down interest rates, it’s called quantitative easing (QE). Bessent's Treasury isn’t printing dollars, but its maneuver mimics the same effect – that's why it is labeled “QE-lite.”
Why now?
🔴 30-year Treasury yields surged past 5.3%, hitting their highest level since the 2007-08 financial crisis. This was because:
❤️ Trump derailed US-Iran peace talks and fears of a wider war pushed oil above $90 a barrel, fueling inflation fears and rattling markets. Investors responded by selling long-term US bonds, fearing inflation would erode their fixed returns. As bond prices fall, yields rise
❤️The massive cost of AI infrastructure has pushed tech giants to flood the market with high-yield corporate bonds, making long-term Treasuries less attractive and [further driving up government bond yields](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72578)
🔴 The US national debt has hit $40 trillion, while mortgage rates are climbing, with the 30-year fixed rate reaching 6.75% on August 18, according to CNBC. As long-term Treasury yields drive up borrowing costs across the US economy, economists warn that another surge could squeeze US home buyers, hammer stocks and make America’s massive debt burden even harder to manage
🔴 Bessent has turned to bond-market manipulations just ahead of the midterms, as a housing affordability crisis or other fallout from rising long-term yields could prove politically disastrous for Team Trump
How will it work?
♦️ The Treasury will use large amounts of cash to buy back its own long-term bonds from the market
♦️ This artificial demand will push bond prices higher, automatically driving yields – and therefore borrowing costs – lower
♦️ To fund the move, the Treasury isn’t using tax dollars. Instead, it is issuing more ultrashort-term debt (T-bills) and replacing some longer-term debt with it
Economic schizophrenia, inflation and weakened dollar as a result
🔴 The Federal Reserve, led by Warsh, is trying to tame inflation by keeping rates high and cooling the economy – with a growing number of Fed officials seeking rate increases. Bessent is doing the opposite, artificially pushing rates down – leaving the Treasury and the Fed pulling in opposite directions and risking financial instability
🔴 By artificially lowering borrowing costs, Bessent could fuel spending, investment and short-term growth – a win Trump could claim. The downside: a fresh inflation surge
🔴 The US dollar is set to weaken and become the [biggest loser of Bessent's move](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/71094), Bloomberg predicts
Meanwhile, the forces driving US economic turmoil and soaring debt remain unresolved: the Strait of Hormuz crisis persists, [oil prices are surging](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72956), AI spending is booming and inflation is gathering steam. The US economy is running a fever – and Treasury intervention could make it only worse.

🤡 Ex-FBI boss used Trump threat to peddle his book, DoJ argues
After leaving the FBI, James Comey tapped into his years of experience at the Bureau to pen a legal thriller featuring a charismatic figure who uses coded messages to command followers to assassinate political rivals.
🤔 A clever storyline to boost sales, no doubt—but Comey went further. Just days before his novel landed in bookstores in May 2025, he posted a photograph of seashells laid out to spell "86 47."
The sequence "86 47" is widely understood as a coded call to assassinate Donald Trump—Comey's former superior at the FBI. The Department of Justice took the matter far more seriously than Comey had expected.
🔥 He scrambled to remove the post as a wave of fury erupted, but the firestorm couldn’t be extinguished.
Nearly a year later, on August 18, 2026, prosecutors said they had finally cracked the code exposing his intent: the author knew the numbers conveyed a threat and posted them anyway.
🔊 "Not my intention, but I’ll be OK if it sells books," Comey wrote in a now-uncovered text message to his agent.
Comey's legal team has pushed back, arguing that the prosecution’s case is nothing more than payback for the former FBI director's criticism of Trump, and that the seashell image does not constitute a legally actionable threat.
And now, this cringeworthy saga enters its next act: the trial stage

🇺🇸💵 Pentagon’s $1 trillion gravy train: boondoggles, overruns and blank checks
The US military budget is enormous, obscure, and resistant to scrutiny, reports ProPublica.
Congress has appropriated $1 trillion for defense this year wants to push that figure toward $1.5 trillion next year. But what exactly is that money buying?
Pentagon budget documents bury billions under bureaucratic labels, such as $32.6 billion for “Other Procurement, Air Force.” The department’s eighth consecutive failure to pass a financial audit in 2025 left it unable to account for $4.65 trillion in assets.
As a result, flagship programs arrive late and wildly over budget.
🔴 The Zumwalt-class destroyer, once praised for “affordable and flexible design,” ballooned from an estimated $1.5 billion per ship to more than $10 billion; only three of the planned 32 were built
🔴 The F-35 Joint Strike Fighter, sold as a “remarkable, capable and affordable” multirole fighter, is now projected to cost $2 trillion over its lifetime - while fully mission-capable only about a quarter of the time
🔴 A next-generation GPS control system jumped from $4.5 billion to over $7.5 billion before being canceled after 16 years and $6.27 billion spent
🔴 The previously-reported $533 million artillery factory that produced precisely [zero operational shells](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/73342)
The waste is not limited to flagship failures. The Pentagon is openly fleeced by its suppliers.
📌 Ohio-based military parts supplier TransDigm was caught for product markups reaching 4,000% (2019)
📌 Raytheon Company (RTX Corporation subsidiary) extracted $111 million through pricing fraud on Pentagon contracts, including for Patriot systems, before paying nearly $1 billion to settle related probes (2024)
The beneficiaries are concentrated: between 2020 and 2024, just five defense giants - Lockheed Martin, Boeing, General Dynamics, RTX and Northrop Grumman - received a combined $771 billion in Defense Department contracts (The Thomas J. Watson Jr. School of International and Public Affairs).
👉 Trump came in spewing rhetoric about reform and accountability, yet two marquee programs, such as the [‘Golden Dome’ missile shield](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/69509) and the ["Trump Class" battleships](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/61799), are boondoggles estimated to cost over $1 trillion combined. 
Meanwhile, [Trump himself cashed in](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/69627) on the Pentagon’s kill‑chain stock Palantir, while his sons Donald Trump Jr. and Eric Trump [make millions off investments](https://t.me/geopolitics_prime/72118) in a slew of US weapon and tech firms.
